intro: A phasor measurement unit (PMU) measures voltage and current as phasors. A phasor gives two numbers for the alternating wave: its size, and its angle, which says how far it runs ahead of or behind a perfect 50 Hz reference wave that starts at every UTC second (UTC: the world's standard time). The PMU's clock comes from GPS satellites, so every value has an exact time stamp. A phasor data concentrator (PDC) collects the streams of many PMUs and lines them up by time, to see the whole grid at one instant.
plain: Mains electricity swings back and forth 50 or 60 times a second, depending on the country. C37.118 lets measuring devices across a grid report, many times a second, how strong that swing is and exactly where it is in its rhythm. Each device sets its clock by satellite, so readings from far apart can be laid side by side, like photos taken by many cameras at the same instant. Together they show the whole grid at one moment, and trouble as it spreads.

connect.title: Open the connection
connect.text: The PDC in the control center opens a TCP connection (a reliable link between two computers) to the PMU on port 4712. The PMU sends nothing until it is asked.

config.title: Ask for the configuration
config.text: Data frames, the messages that carry the measurements, hold numbers only: no names, no units. So the PDC first asks for configuration frame 2 (CFG-2). It says which values come, in which format, at which rate.

start.title: Start the stream
start.text: Command 2 turns the data frames on. The PMU sends them until the PDC sends command 1 or closes the connection.

stream.title: 50 frames a second
stream.text: Every 20 ms a data frame arrives with a time stamp, a status, two phasors and the frequency. In 20 ms both angles moved +0.144°. The reason: the grid runs at 50.020 Hz, a little faster than the 50 Hz reference wave.

event.title: A generator trips
event.text: Somewhere in the grid a large generator trips: it suddenly disconnects. The frequency falls: 49.946 Hz, at −0.12 Hz per second. All PMUs time-stamp to the same GPS second, so the PDC can compare their values sample by sample.

frames.cfg2: One PMU, 2 phasors as floats, 50 frames a second

notes.tcp: Plain TCP. Commands and data can share this one connection, as here. A PMU can also send its data over UDP, usually to port 4713. UDP also allows multicast: one stream sent to several PDCs at once.

sync-cmd.name: SYNC
sync-cmd.note: 0xAA starts every frame. 0x41: frame type 4 (a command), version 1 (the frame format of the 2005 standard, which 2011 keeps for these frames).

size-18.name: FRAMESIZE
size-18.note: 18 bytes: the whole frame, the check included.

idcode.name: IDCODE
idcode.note: Data stream 7. A command carries the stream it is for; every other frame carries its own.

tq-0.name: Time quality
tq-0.note: 0: the clock is locked to UTC and no leap second is due. If GPS fails, this code says how far off the clock may be.

frac-954.name: FRACSEC
frac-954.note: The fraction of the second, in millionths: 0x0E8E90 = 954 000 µs: 10:41:06.954.

frac-0.name: FRACSEC
frac-0.note: 0: exactly on the second. This is when the values were measured, not when the frame left.

frac-20.name: FRACSEC
frac-20.note: 0x004E20 = 20 000 µs: 20 ms after the second, one frame later.

cmd-5.name: CMD 5
cmd-5.note: Send configuration frame 2. Other commands: 1 stops the data, 2 starts it, 3 asks for the header frame, 4 for CFG-1.

chk.name: CHK
chk.note: An error check (CRC-CCITT) over every byte before it: polynomial 0x1021, start value 0xFFFF. A frame with a wrong check is thrown away.

timebase.name: TIME_BASE
timebase.note: 1 000 000 (0x0F4240): FRACSEC counts millionths of a second.

numpmu.name: NUM_PMU
numpmu.note: 1 PMU in this stream. A PDC that forwards many PMUs lists them all here, and its data frames carry one block for each.

pad.name: Padding
pad.note: Spaces: every name in CFG-2 is exactly 16 characters long.

pmuid.name: IDCODE
pmuid.note: The ID of this PMU's data: 7.

format.name: FORMAT
format.note: 0x000B: phasors as floats in polar form (magnitude and angle). FREQ and DFREQ (the frequency and its rate of change) are floats too.

counts.name: PHNMR · ANNMR · DGNMR
counts.note: 2 phasors, 0 analog values, 0 digital status words. With FORMAT, this fixes the size of every data frame.

chnam-v.name: CHNAM
chnam-v.note: The name of phasor 1: V1 POS SEQ, the positive-sequence voltage (the three phases combined into one balanced value).

chnam-i.name: CHNAM
chnam-i.note: Phasor 2: I1 POS SEQ, the positive-sequence current.

phunit-v.name: PHUNIT
phunit-v.note: First byte 0: phasor 1 is a voltage. The other 3 bytes scale 16-bit integers (300 000 × 10⁻⁵ V per bit); with floats they are ignored.

phunit-i.name: PHUNIT
phunit-i.note: First byte 1: phasor 2 is a current. 3 000 × 10⁻⁵ A per bit, also unused with floats.

fnom.name: FNOM
fnom.note: The nominal frequency. Bit 0 set: a 50 Hz grid. Clear, it would mean 60 Hz.

cfgcnt.name: CFGCNT
cfgcnt.note: 3: the PMU's configuration has been changed 3 times. The PDC compares it to know whether its copy is current.

rate.name: DATA_RATE
rate.note: 50 frames per second: one every 20 ms.

stat.name: STAT
stat.note: 0x0000: data good, PMU in sync with UTC, sorted by time stamp, no trigger, no configuration change coming.

v1-mag-0.name: V1 magnitude
v1-mag-0.note: 89 120 V, a float, measured from phase to neutral. Between two phases that is about 154 kV.

v1-ang-0.name: V1 angle
v1-ang-0.note: −0.21642 rad = −12.400°, against the 50 Hz reference wave.

dfreq-0.name: DFREQ
dfreq-0.note: The rate of change of frequency: 0.000 Hz/s.

i1-mag-ev.name: I1 magnitude
i1-mag-ev.note: 455.0 A: the line now carries more power.

freq-ev.name: FREQ
freq-ev.note: 49.946 Hz: below 50 Hz, because the grid lost a generator.

facts.standard: IEEE C37.118.2-2011 (the frames); the measurement itself: IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1
facts.between: PMU → PDC, PDC → PDC and applications
facts.transport: TCP 4712 for commands, and often data; UDP 4713 for data
facts.security: None: a CRC only. Use a separate network or a VPN. IEC 61850-90-5 is the secured alternative.
facts.speed: 10 to 50 frames per second on a 50 Hz grid. Time within about 1 µs of UTC: 1 µs is 0.018° at 50 Hz.

tips: Data frames carry no names and no units. If the PMU's setup changes and the PDC keeps the old CFG-2, it reads wrong values without an error. STAT bit 10 warns before a change: then read CFG-2 again.
Check the time quality before you trust an angle. When GPS is lost, STAT bit 13 is set and the angles drift: 1 ms of clock error is 18° at 50 Hz.
The IDCODE must match on both sides. A PDC set up for stream 7 ignores frames that carry another number.
Angles are only comparable at the same time stamp. A PDC waits a set time for late frames: too short and it drops data, too long and every display lags.

timing.title: Every frame is tied to the UTC second
timing.note: The PMU measures at fixed moments: 0, 20, 40 ms … after each UTC second, as its GPS clock marks it. The frame leaves a little later, here 30 ms. The time stamp is the moment of the measurement, so a PDC can line up PMUs whose frames arrive at different times.

playground.encoder: C37.118 sends floats most significant (highest) byte first (ABCD). 89120 is the V1 magnitude of the first data frame: 47 AE 10 00.
